title: Minimum Domino Rotations For Equal Row
statement:
A line of dominoes is described by two equal-length arrays: domino `i` shows `tops[i]` on its upper half and `bottoms[i]` on its lower half, each a number from 1 to 6. Rotating domino `i` exchanges its two halves, swapping `tops[i]` with `bottoms[i]`.

Return the fewest rotations after which every entry of `tops` is the same number, or every entry of `bottoms` is the same number (either row is enough). Return `-1` if no sequence of rotations achieves this.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying all six values for both rows works, but there is a sharper observation: whatever value fills a row in the end must appear on every domino, including the first one. So the only candidates are `tops[0]` and `bottoms[0]`. For a fixed candidate the greedy choice is forced: a domino already showing it in the chosen row stays, any other domino must be rotated, and a domino without it on either half makes the candidate impossible.

## Approach

1. Start `best` at `Infinity`.
2. For each `target` in `[tops[0], bottoms[0]]`, scan every domino `i`.
3. If neither half shows `target`, mark the candidate impossible and stop the scan.
4. Otherwise count `topSwaps` (dominoes whose top is not `target`, which need a rotation to fix the top row) and `bottomSwaps` (the same for the bottom row).
5. If the candidate is possible, lower `best` to the smaller of the two counts.
6. Return `-1` if `best` was never lowered, else `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`tops = [2,1,2,4,2,2]`, `bottoms = [5,2,6,2,3,2]`. Target `2`: every domino shows a 2 somewhere. Tops at indices 1 and 3 are not 2, so `topSwaps = 2`; bottoms at indices 0, 2 and 4 are not 2, so `bottomSwaps = 3`. `best` becomes 2. Target `5`: domino 1 is `(1, 2)`, with no 5, so this candidate fails. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): at most two passes over the dominoes.
- Space: O(1): a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- Count rotations for both rows; the bottom row may be the cheaper one.
- A domino showing `target` on both halves never needs a rotation and must not be counted.
- If `tops[0] === bottoms[0]` both passes test the same value; that is harmless.
- Return `-1`, not `Infinity` or `0`, when neither candidate works.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | fewest rotations found so far |
| `target` | the value we try to fill a row with |
| `topSwaps` | rotations needed to make every top equal `target` |
| `bottomSwaps` | rotations needed to make every bottom equal `target` |
| `possible` | whether every domino shows `target` on some half |
